question: In the rate test, what capacities did NFA-A and NFA-F recover at 0.1C after the 1C step, against their initial 0.1C capacities, and what losses does the paper give for each?
expect: NFA-A ~170 vs ~184 mAh/g ('similar (~5%)'); NFA-F ~138 vs ~190 mAh/g (~27% loss) (p10.L37-43). 170/184 is a 7.6% loss, larger than the stated ~5%
rendered:
According to the text, after the 1C step, the NFA-A variant recovered a capacity of ≈170 mAh g−1 at 0.1C, which is similar (≈5%) to the initial capacity of ≈184 mAh g−1 observed at 0.1C prior to the rate capability tests.

The NFA-F variant delivered a low capacity of ≈138 mAh g−1 at 0.1C after the 1C step, which resulted in ≈27% loss compared to the initial capacity of ≈190 mAh g−1.

source.file: Advanced Materials - 2020 - Muralidharan - Lithium Iron Aluminum Nickelate  LiNixFeyAlzO2 New Sustainable Cathodes for.pdf
